subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session hook-agent deliveries be rejected with 409, skipped, queued, or left accepted by default, and should any non-parallel behavior be opt-in per hook or mapping?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the public webhook response contract and retry semantics, while the available alternatives create different compatibility, queueing, and operator-control tradeoffs that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Preserve accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved sessionKey.

options.title: Make 409 The Default
options.body: Reject active same-session hook deliveries by default and accept that existing webhook producers may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Leave Locking To Callers
options.body: Keep OpenClaw’s hook endpoint accepted-by-default and document idempotency keys plus caller-managed locks as the supported overlap control.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Preserve accepted-by-default behavior and add a documented hook or mapping policy for reject, skip, or queue semantics keyed by the resolved sessionKey.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties this person to the hook request-handler and session admission path that would need the policy boundary.
